currentContext.business: Jain Resource Recycling Limited ('JRRL') recycles and processes non-ferrous scrap - lead scrap and lead-acid batteries, copper wires, cables and scrap, aluminium scrap, tin-bearing streams and cable plastics - into refined and remelted ingots, billets, alloys and granules at integrated manufacturing facilities at Gummidipoondi, Chennai, supported by a global procurement network spanning more than 120 countries. It runs a B2B model supplying recycled non-ferrous metals and by-products to approximately 371 clients across over 20 countries, with exports contributing about 62% of total turnover; domestic marquee clients named are Vedanta, Amara Raja Batteries, Luminous Power Technologies, HBL Batteries and Chloride Metals, and international clients named are Mitsubishi Corporation, Nissan Trading, Trafigura, IXM SA, Toko Company and Hodaka. Building on this platform it is moving downstream into higher-value copper products - cathodes, wire rods and busbars.

Lead & Lead Alloy Ingots: 'JAIN 9997' - lead brand registered with the LME and approved by MCX
Aluminium & Aluminium Ingots: Molten Aluminium Alloy (supplied in hot molten form since 2018)
Plastics: Recycled PP and PVC granules (sold to plastic product manufacturers)
Solder Tin Alloy & Tin Ingots: Solder tin alloy and tin ingots (tin refining operations commenced 2025)

currentContext.expansion: JRRL's expansion programme in FY 2025-26 is built around copper forward integration, raw-material security and by-product value extraction. Copper anode production commenced in March 2026 at Jain Green Technologies Unit 3, marking entry into value-added copper manufacturing; a second furnace in an advanced stage of installation is to take total anode capacity to 1,600 MT per month by Q1 FY 2026-27. Civil construction of the cathode facility is complete, with Phase 1 and Phase 2 commissioning targeted for Q2 and Q3 FY 2026-27 respectively, and wire rod and busbar commissioning following in August and September 2026; management expects the integrated platform to lift copper segment EBITDA margins by approximately 200-400 basis points. On sourcing, the Jain CY Circular Solutions joint venture with C&Y Group Investments Inc. will run an Ahmedabad facility planned to process 72,000 MT of scrap annually and generate approximately 25,000 MT of copper output per annum - factory premises finalised on lease, implementation underway, operations phased from September 2026. In lead, a 25% equity stake in M/s. Abraj Al Khaleej, Kuwait gives right-of-first-refusal access to Middle East recycled material and is expected to be operational through FY 2026-27, with minor timeline slippage attributed to shipping-route disruption. By-product value extraction advanced on two fronts: tin recovery capacity was raised from 125 MTPA to 500 MTPA during the year after installing an additional vacuum distillation furnace, and a proposed antimony extraction plant (estimated capex approximately Rs 20 Crores) is targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY 2026-27. A dedicated standalone plastic recycling unit of approximately six acres, estimated capex Rs 15 Crores, is also slated for Q3 FY 2026-27 commissioning to decongest plastic processing and turn it into an independent profit centre. The Directors' Report frames the same programme as 'strengthening its presence in the downstream metals segment through expansion into higher-value products, including copper cathodes, wire rods, and busbars', from integrated facilities at Gummidipoondi, Chennai. Environment-linked capex during the year comprised the installation of a Primary and Secondary Air Pollution Control System for the Rotary Furnace to reduce emissions and improve ambient air quality (BRSR Principle 2). NOTE ON THAT BRSR ROW: it reports environment/social capex as 0.31% of total capex for FY 2025-26 (FY 2024-25: Nil) but the Company's own footnote immediately contradicts the number - 'The Company has not separately tracked the percentage of R&D and capital expenditure investments attributable to environmental and social impact initiatives. Accordingly, the percentage is reported as NR I.E., Not Recorded.' The 0.31% is therefore not relied on and is not carried into capex_disclosed (it is also a percentage, not a rupee quantum, and did not arrive under a NAMED DISCLOSURE heading).

risks.risk: Commodity price volatility (LME lead, copper, aluminium)
risks.note: MD&A 'Market and Financial' risk: fluctuations in global market prices for lead, copper and aluminium directly impact revenue and gross margins. Mitigation is a disciplined LME hedging mechanism with sales prices monitored against raw-material procurement. The structural exposure is visible in management's own Q4 commentary (sibling bundles): a short-window surge in LME copper compressed realisations because the industry's formula-based pricing expresses price as a percentage of LME.

risks.risk: Raw material insecurity - dependence on scrap availability
risks.note: MD&A 'Operational' risk: dependence on scrap availability, both domestic and imported, heightens sensitivity to supply-side disruption, quality variation, logistics delays and price volatility. Mitigated by a diversified sourcing network; domestic sourcing was raised to approximately 39% of volume during the year to cut dependence on long-lead-time imports. The remaining ~61% import dependence is the structural residue.

MD&A 'Market and Financial' risk: significant international trade in US Dollars and Euros creates currency risk. Managed by monitoring net exposures and using forward contracts, with a partial natural hedge to the extent import and export flows align.

risks.risk: Operational safety in molten-metal and hazardous-material handling
risks.note: MD&A 'Operational' risk and the top-ranked BRSR material issue: recycling, smelting, refining and handling of molten metals are safety-sensitive; recycling operations involve heavy machinery and hazardous materials posing injury risk to the workforce. Stated financial implication is negative - potential medical compensation, legal costs and operational downtime. Mitigated by safety policies, risk assessments, safety manuals, PPE, mandatory training and ISO 45001:2018 certification.

risks.risk: Geopolitical instability, shipping-route and trade disruption
risks.note: MD&A 'Strategic and External' risk: conflicts, trade policy changes, port disruptions or restrictions in key sourcing and export regions can affect procurement, logistics and market access. This risk has already crystallised twice in the year on management's own account - a freight/logistics cost spike on import containers, and delay to the Kuwait (Abraj Al Khaleej) project timeline.

MD&A 'Financial' risk: timely scrap procurement, inventory holding, receivables management and funding support are critical in a volatile commodity environment. Managed through internal controls, treasury processes and management review. Structurally amplified by global sourcing, commodity-linked pricing and the working-capital-intensive nature of recycling.

risks.risk: Environmental and EPR regulatory compliance, and GHG/energy intensity
risks.note: MD&A 'Regulatory and ESG' risk (mitigation text TRUNCATED mid-sentence at 'The Company' in the routed extract) plus BRSR material issue #2: energy-intensive recycling processes increase the carbon footprint and expose the Company to stringent climate regulation, with stated negative financial implications of potential carbon taxes, compliance penalties and capital expenditure for upgrades. Evolving EPR frameworks and hazardous waste rules raise compliance requirements; management notes EPR regulations take effect from April 2026.

MD&A 'Operational' risk: strict technical specifications across lead, copper and aluminium must be met to avoid rejections, cancellations or customer dissatisfaction. Mitigated by multi-stage quality control including microstructure and spectrometer analysis before dispatch.

BRSR Principle 1 disclosure: SEBI levied a monetary penalty in a case alleging that the Chairman and the Jain Family Trust traded shares of Refex Industries Limited while in possession of unpublished price-sensitive information under the SEBI PIT Regulations (the Company clarifies the allegations do not concern its own shares); the Securities Appellate Tribunal admitted the appeal against SEBI's order dated 12 December 2025 and stayed recovery subject to a 50% deposit. Read with the FY26 Secretarial Audit observations disclosed in the Directors' Report (sibling bundle) - a Regulation 32 deviation on IPO fund utilisation towards repayment of a promoter loan, and Regulation 23 related-party transactions with the Chairman & MD entered without prior/omnibus Audit Committee approval - this is a live governance watch-item for a company in its first year as a listed entity.

risks.note: BRSR material issue #6 (Risk): inefficient resource utilisation, particularly of water and process waste, threatens operational resilience, with negative financial implications from escalating water procurement costs and higher waste disposal levies. Mitigation is closed-loop water recycling systems and maximised secondary material recovery efficiency.

Structural people risk visible in BRSR Section A (routed to sibling bundles): the workforce is 443 permanent employees but 1,350 workers all of whom are 'other than permanent' (permanent workers: 0), and permanent-employee turnover was 16% in FY 2025-26 with female turnover at 36%. Board diversity is thin - 1 woman among 8 directors (12.5%) and 0 among 4 KMP. [PROVENANCE: BRSR Section A items 20-22 arrived in the profile/governance/registry bundles, not in risks_esg.]

one-line thesis: Jain Resource Recycling delivered record FY26 growth with 48% revenue and 56% PAT growth, driven by scale and hedging discipline, but Q4 EBITDA per ton was temporarily compressed by $4K copper LME volatility and $6K logistics shocks; management has fixed the formula mechanism and is now executing $120Cr capex to integrate copper anode/cathode/wire rod/busbar production, transforming earnings from cyclical recycling to stable value-added margins.
financial scorecard: revenue: +48% YoY (INR9,543Cr); EBITDA/margin: +53% YoY to INR559Cr (5.9% margin); PAT (rptd): +56% YoY to INR347Cr; PAT (normalized): +56% YoY (no material distortions); order book: N/A (no formal order book); net debt: INR375Cr IPO proceeds used to repay debt, leverage maintained healthy
guidance: revenue growth: double-digit (copper >15%, lead 10-15%); margin: normalized EBITDA per ton copper INR30K-32K/ton; order inflow: none specified; capex/commissioning: INR115-120Cr in FY27, with cathode (Q2FY27), wire rod (Aug26), busbar (Sep26), Ahmedabad (Dec26), Kuwait (post-shipping normalization), plastic plant (Q3FY27)
segment / subsidiary detail: Copper & alloys: 55% of revenue; Lead & alloys: 40%; Aluminium: 5%; Exports: 62%; Domestic: 38%
growth verticals / optionality: Copper cathode/wire rod/busbar integration; Antimony recovery from lead scrap; Dedicated plastic recycling unit; Kuwait JV for Middle East scrap access; Potential expansion into other specialty metals
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 FY26 EBITDA per ton copper compressed by INR18.5K due to LME formula volatility and INR6K due to shipping/logistics; normalized EBITDA per ton copper guidance: INR30K-32K; cost normalization expected in Q1FY27
capex / expansion: INR115-120Cr in FY27: Copper cathode phase 2 (INR40Cr est.), Ahmedabad JV (INR30Cr), Kuwait JV (INR30Cr), plastic recycling plant (INR15Cr), antimony recovery (INR20Cr)
capital allocation: INR375Cr of INR500Cr IPO proceeds used for debt repayment; remaining INR125Cr for capex and corporate purposes; no dividend policy disclosed; focus on capex-funded value-addition over buybacks
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical shipping disruptions (Iran/Strait of Hormuz); copper LME volatility (mitigated by new hedging mechanism); project execution delays; raw material sourcing concentration in transshipment hubs (UAE); antimony recovery tech risk
management quality / tone: Confident, forward-looking, disciplined; acknowledged Q4 headwinds as transitory; emphasized structural shift from recycling to integrated value chain; proactive on hedging reform and capex execution
non-obvious takeaways: Copper formula volatility is a market-wide phenomenon (not company-specific), akin to oil refining margins; plastic recycling is purely byproduct-driven (no virgin plastic); Kuwait project is critical for lead scrap security, not just copper; antimony recovery is a high-margin specialty metal play hidden in lead recycling
